critical_code_review_comments: openWallet() architecture is sound: directly mutates DY.pagina + DY._laatstGerenderd + DY.brandPortal._renderLock, pushes history state with ?pagina=wallet, then calls renderWallet() locally — fully bypasses DY.navigeer/DY.toonPagina/brand-portal _renderLock guard/pp-nav-fix wrap chain.

Idempotency: openWallet may be invoked twice (capture-phase delegator fires first, inline onclick second). renderWallet uses DOM overwrites (innerHTML/appendChild/querySelector) — safe to re-run rapidly.

rca of the issue: Reported bug: even with correct v60.1.158 inline onclick the user still saw B2C packages. Root cause hypothesised: brand-portal-v1.js _renderLock guard (lines 211-215) silently aborts non-BP_PAGES navigation during a 2s render window, and pp-nav-fix-v1.js wraps DY.toonPagina. Any DY.navigeer('wallet') call could be absorbed by these legacy wrappers before reaching renderWallet. Mitigation in v60.1.159: PP_Wallet.openWallet() short-circuits the entire chain — it mutates DY state directly (DY.pagina='wallet', DY._laatstGerenderd=null, DY.brandPortal._renderLock=false), pushes history state, then invokes the local renderWallet() reference (not via DY.navigeer/DY.toonPagina). Both the inline onclick and the document-level capture-phase delegator now invoke openWallet() first (with full backwards-compatible navigeer fallback). Backwards compatibility: if PP_Wallet is undefined or openWallet throws, fallback to legacy DY.navigeer('wallet') path is preserved. ZERO breaking change to B2C wallet, brand-portal-v1.js, or pp-nav-fix-v1.js.
